title: Incident Knowledge Bus and Warm Handoff Runbook
author: Sofia Martinez
body:
Overview:

This runbook documents the Incident Knowledge Bus (IKB) concept and the warm-handoff procedure used for multi-shift and cross-team incident transitions. The IKB is a lightweight, structured incident artifact that lives for the duration of an incident (and is retained for postmortem evidence). It standardizes what information must be captured, how responders hand off context, and how game days exercise handoffs.

Objectives:
- Reduce cognitive load during shift changes by providing a single source of truth for in-flight incidents.
- Ensure consistent, auditable information for post-incident reviews and regulatory evidence.
- Make warm handoffs fast (<= 10 minutes) while preserving technical depth for follow-ups.

When to use this runbook:
1. Any incident declared P1 or P2 that will span more than one on-call shift.
2. Degradations involving model quality regressions, KV cache corruption, or cross-region capacity blips.
3. Game day scenarios where handoff timing and fidelity are being evaluated.

Key concept: Incident Knowledge Bus (IKB)
- Definition: A short-lived document + metadata bundle (JSON payload) stored in the incident evidence bucket and mirrored to the incident Slack channel by the bridge operator.
- Lifetime: Created at incident declaration; appended during major events (new mitigation, rollback, scale action); finalized at incident resolution and retained per retention policy.
- Consumers: bridge operator, on-call engineer taking over, QA/ML SME, SRE lead, customer success for customer-facing messaging.

IKB Minimum Schema (human-readable summary + machine fields) - example payload (abbreviated):

```json
{
  "incident_id": "INC-2026-1234",
  "severity": "P1",
  "summary": "Elevated 95thpct latency and token drop for model-x in us-west-2",
  "first_detection_ts": "2026-03-01T21:12:00Z",
  "current_status": "stabilized, partial rollback in progress",
  "action_log": [
    {"ts":"2026-03-01T21:15:10Z","actor":"oncall-ingress","action":"scaled-gpu-pool","note":"+20% burst"},
    {"ts":"2026-03-01T21:30:45Z","actor":"ml-sre","action":"rollback-model","note":"rolled back to v2.1.3"}
  ],
  "key_metrics_at_decl": {"p50_latency_ms":"120","p95_latency_ms":"790","error_rate":"2.8%"},
  "evidence_links": ["s3://redwood-incident-evidence/INC-2026-1234/logs.zip","https://grafana.company/incident/1234"],
  "handoff_required": true
}
```

Warm Handoff Procedure (target duration: 5-10 minutes)
1) Declare and create: The bridge operator confirms incident ID and posts the initial IKB payload to #incidents-bridge and the incident Slack channel. Use `incident-bus create --id <INC-ID> --summary "..."` (CLI example below).
2) Capture state: The outgoing responder updates the IKB with the current state, last mitigation attempted, and top-3 open action items (owner + ETA).
3) Quick context brief (2–3 minutes): Outgoing responder provides a verbal summary on the bridge: impact, mitigations so far, known unknowns, and one-sentence recommended next step.
4) Sanity check (3–5 minutes): Incoming responder reviews IKB fields, validates evidence links (grafana/dashboards), and runs the two verification commands listed in the checklist.
5) Ownership transfer: Incoming responder posts acknowledgment in Slack with the snippet: "ACK takeover: <name> - will own until <time/UTC>. Stabilization goal: <goal metric>. See IKB: <s3 link>". Bridge operator pins final IKB link.
6) Update ticketing: Update incident ticket/PD incident with new owner and mark handoff time.
7) Close loop: After 15 minutes, if there is no major change, outgoing responder writes a 1–3 bullet note summarizing any deferred investigations and the rationale.

Handoff checklist (commands and artifacts) - minimum required before ACK:
- Evidence links: grafana snapshot, argo logs link, model metrics dashboard, recent S3 log bundle.
- Run these two quick checks (copy/paste to bridge):
  - `curl -sS https://internal-health.api/serving/model-x/health | jq .` (expect `"status":"healthy"`)
  - `rdctl metrics tail --window 60s --filter "model:model-x" --format summary` (verify p95 and error rate)
- Attach recent KV cache summary: `kv-dump --shard all --head 1h > kv-head.json` and upload to evidence bucket.
- List of top 3 suspects and reproducibility steps (if applicable).
- Customer impact classification and template to use for status page (Template A/B/C below).

Customer Status Templates (short, copy/paste with placeholders)
- Template A (P1, wide customer impact):
  "We are aware of an issue affecting Redwood API (model generation latency) in <region>. Our engineers are actively working on a fix. Current status: partial degradation; customers may experience timeouts or increased latency. Next update: <ETA-30m>. Incident ID: <INC-ID>.
- Template B (P2, limited customers):
  "We are investigating elevated latency for specific model variants in <region>. If you see errors, please contact support and include Incident ID <INC-ID>. Next update: <ETA-60m>.
- Template C (informational):
  "We observed transient errors for a small percentage of requests to <endpoint>. A rollback/patch has been applied and services are returning to normal. No action required."

Post-incident Knowledge Transfer (within 72 hours)
- Required artifacts: finalized IKB, timeline (one-line per action), postmortem draft, list of follow-ups with owners and due dates, customer impact summary and credits (if any).
- Follow-up meeting format: 30-minute synthesis with SRE, ML, platform, and customer success. Agenda: timeline & evidence, root cause hypotheses, mitigating controls, and remediation plan.
- Artifact retention: All IKB payloads and evidence links are retained per `security-and-compliance/data-retention-incident-policy` (default 2 years for P1).

Game day integration: exercising handoffs
- Goal: validate that warm handoffs meet the <=10 minute target and that incoming responders can resume mitigation from the IKB alone.
- Scenario design: craft an incident that intentionally spans two shifts (e.g., inject model degradation at T0+20m).
- Scoring rubric:
  - IKB completeness (0-5) - fields filled, evidence links valid.
  - Handoff speed (0-5) - <5m full score; 5–10m partial; >10m fail.
  - Action continuity (0-5) - incoming responder successfully continues mitigation without additional SME.
- Post-game updates: annotate the IKB with game-day notes and a retro entry. Use label `game-day:YYYY-MM` on the IKB bucket object.

Automation & CLI examples
- Create IKB: `incident-bus create --id INC-2026-1234 --severity P1 --summary "Elevated p95 latency model-x" --evidence https://grafana/...`
- Append action: `incident-bus append --id INC-2026-1234 --actor ml-sre --action "rollback model" --note "v2.1.3"`
- Snapshot evidence to S3: `incident-collector snapshot --incident INC-2026-1234 --dashboards grafana.* --out s3://redwood-incident-evidence/INC-2026-1234/logs.zip`
- Slack post helper: `incident-bus post-slack --id INC-2026-1234 --channel #incidents-bridge`

Edge cases and rules of thumb
- If the incoming responder cannot validate evidence links within 5 minutes due to access errors, escalate to bridge operator to request temporary access; do not accept handoff without verifiable evidence for P1 incidents.
- When an incident has regulatory implications (customer data exfil suspicion), mark `confidentiality: restricted` and notify Security & Legal immediately.
- For incidents involving model quality regressions, include a reproducibility artifact (prompt + seed + model-variant) in the IKB.

Responsibilities and ownership
- Bridge operator: create and pin IKB; coordinate cross-team comms; manage channel hygiene.
- Outgoing on-call: populate baseline IKB fields and confirm evidence links.
- Incoming on-call: validate, ACK, and assume ownership in ticketing and Slack.
- SRE lead / incident commander: ensure IKB exists for any incident that will last longer than one shift.

Runbook maintenance
- Owner: Eng SRE knowledge team (document owner: Sofia Martinez).
- Review cadence: quarterly review and after every P1 postmortem for correctness.
- Game day refresh: annual scenario refresh with Product and ML to simulate new failure modes.

Appendix: Quick checklist paste (for bridge operator)
1) `incident-bus create --id <INC-ID> --summary "..."`
2) Post IKB link in #incidents-bridge and pin.
3) Instruct outgoing to run KV + metrics checks and upload.
4) Request ACK from incoming with owner timestamp.
5) After handoff, outgoing posts deferred investigation bullets.

This runbook is intentionally prescriptive for P1/P2 cases to keep handoffs predictable and evidence-rich. For smaller incidents (P3/P4) teams may use a lightweight IKB with only summary/evidence links and a single-line ACK on Slack.
